done_state: Given dim_project/project_root state and a list of cwd values, resolve rebuilds cwd_project (and cwd_project_candidate for ambiguous cases) using path-component-aware longest-match matching ARCHITECTURE.md section 3's design exactly: never a bare string prefix, correctly ambiguous when two projects tie at the same depth, correctly unregistered when nothing matches, honoring a .foreman/tessera-prefix override when present, and idempotent -- re-running against unchanged registry state or a changed one always leaves cwd_project consistent with the CURRENT registry, never a stale prior answer.

criteria.statement: Matching is path-component-aware, never a bare string prefix: a registered root that is a literal string prefix of another real, differently-registered path (e.g. /path/to/example-project vs /path/to/example-project-ft) must not match the wrong one just because the string overlaps.
criteria.verification: atlas/resolve/tests/test_matching.py: registers two projects at /proj/example-project and /proj/example-project-ft; resolves a cwd of /proj/example-project-ft/src; asserts it resolves uniquely to the example-project-ft project, not ambiguously or to example-project.

criteria.statement: A cwd matching exactly one registered root at the longest matching depth resolves unique, with matched_root, project_prefix, and candidate_count=1 all correctly populated.
criteria.verification: atlas/resolve/tests/test_matching.py: registers one project, resolves a cwd nested under its root, asserts resolution='unique' and the CHECK-constraint-implied triple is consistent.

criteria.statement: A cwd matching two or more registered roots at the SAME longest depth (the real AREM/FORE shape: two projects sharing one source_root) resolves ambiguous, with all candidates recorded in cwd_project_candidate and project_prefix NULL in cwd_project.
criteria.verification: atlas/resolve/tests/test_matching.py: registers two projects at the identical source_root, resolves a cwd equal to that root, asserts resolution='ambiguous', candidate_count=2, and both prefixes present in cwd_project_candidate.

criteria.statement: A cwd matching no registered root resolves unregistered, with matched_root and project_prefix both NULL and candidate_count=0.
criteria.verification: atlas/resolve/tests/test_matching.py: resolves a cwd under no registered root, asserts resolution='unregistered'.

criteria.statement: A .foreman/tessera-prefix override file, when present for a given root, is read and takes precedence over the registry for cwds under that root -- ARCHITECTURE.md section 3's already-decided remedy for the AREM/FORE-shaped ambiguity.
criteria.verification: atlas/resolve/tests/test_override.py: registers two projects sharing one source_root (ambiguous by registry alone); supplies a tessera-prefix override naming one of the two for that root; asserts the cwd now resolves unique to the overridden prefix, not ambiguous.

criteria.statement: Re-running resolve against UNCHANGED registry state is idempotent: no duplicate cwd_project rows, no drift in resolution/matched_root/project_prefix/candidate_count.
criteria.verification: atlas/resolve/tests/test_idempotency.py: runs resolve twice against the same dim_project/project_root/cwd list, asserts cwd_project row count and content are identical before and after the second run.

criteria.statement: A registry CHANGE (a new project_root registered after the first resolve) causes the next resolve run to UPDATE the affected cwd_project rows to the new correct answer, not leave them keyed to the stale pre-change resolution -- ARCHITECTURE.md section 4's 'a registry change re-resolves history rather than leaving rows keyed to a stale answer'.
criteria.verification: atlas/resolve/tests/test_idempotency.py: resolves a cwd as unregistered, registers a new project whose root covers that cwd, re-runs resolve, asserts the SAME cwd_project row (same cwd PK) now reads resolution='unique' with the new project_prefix, not a second stale row.

criteria.statement: Every write resolve makes to cwd_project satisfies its own CHECK constraints (resolution/project_prefix/candidate_count consistency, already enforced by the warehouse schema) -- resolve never needs PRAGMA ignore_check_constraints or a constraint-bypassing write path.
criteria.verification: atlas/resolve/tests/test_matching.py and test_idempotency.py: every resolve call in every test runs against a real migrated warehouse database with all CHECK constraints live (no bypass), and a passing test run is itself the evidence -- a constraint violation would raise and fail the test.

failure_criteria.statement: An ambiguous or unregistered cwd is silently written as if it were the single matching project, or a stale resolution is left in place after a registry change without being corrected.
failure_criteria.detection: Every resolution path (unique/ambiguous/unregistered) has its own asserting test, including the specific re-resolution-after-registry-change case (C7), not just the happy path.

failure_criteria.statement: A resolved-project count or match count in this component's code comments, docstrings, or commit messages has no reproduction path.
failure_criteria.detection: grep the component's source and its commit messages for numeric claims; each must name the command or test that produced it.

failure_criteria.statement: The matcher assumes a root string is well-formed (no trailing slash inconsistency, no symlink resolution) rather than normalizing it, silently producing a false non-match.
failure_criteria.detection: Root and cwd paths are compared via pathlib.Path component lists after normalization, not raw string equality -- a test with a trailing-slash-inconsistent root/cwd pair must still match correctly.

failure_criteria.statement: A malformed or unreadable .foreman/tessera-prefix override is silently ignored, falling back to the registry with no signal that the override was present but broken.
failure_criteria.detection: A malformed override file (unreadable, or naming a prefix not in dim_project) produces a named, observable result the caller/test can see -- not a silent fallback indistinguishable from 'no override file exists'.

out_of_scope: Populating dim_project or project_root from the real TESSERA registry -- that is ingest's job (tessera_to_ingest interface, out of scope in ingest's own GOALS.json too, pending its own criteria); this component consumes whatever rows are already there.
Real end-to-end resolution against the live 35-project registry and 575 real distinct cwds -- this component's tests use synthetic fixtures; end-to-end correctness is foreman:integration-test's job.
Any MAJOR/MINOR finding not specifically about resolve's own matching logic per the QUALITY-BAR triage.
constraints: Zero third-party dependencies -- Python 3 stdlib only (pathlib), matching this environment's established convention.
Matching uses pathlib.Path component comparison, never str.startswith, per ARCHITECTURE.md section 3's explicit requirement and the five real root-pair collisions it names.
Tests use Python's stdlib unittest, matching warehouse/ingest's own convention.
